title: consp
summary: This is a humorous list-style compilation of imaginary government and conspiracy holdings, assembled as a resource for a role-playing game set in a secret U.S. government warehouse. The compiler explains that the idea began with a joke about a 'Ark of the Covenant' box in a warehouse from a TV series, and the list grew to gather items that films, television, folklore, history and conspiracy theories claim were seized and hidden. Entries are one-line or short descriptions, sorted into sections for the American, Soviet, Japanese and Vatican warehouses. Examples include a 100 MPG carburetor, Elvis clones, the Necronomicon, Fermat's notebook, Hitler's photographs, Captain Hook's hand, and a Mona Lisa with a disputed label. The tone is satirical and irreverent, mixing pop culture references, science fiction, historical rumour and jokes at the expense of politicians and conspiracy theorists. The text ends with a closing section that includes a deliberately offensive denialist paragraph, which the record notes as part of the collection's content.
